metadata.case_name: AGACER JAMES C v. ARNOLD ARTHUR JOHN

plaintiff.occupation_after: Part-time private tutor until April 2010; unable to work thereafter

injuries.description: depressed non-comminuted skull fracture over right frontal bone underlying the scalp lacerations.
source: Subsequent CT brain showed depressed non-comminuted skull fracture over right frontal bone underlying the scalp lacerations.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of squama of frontal bone of skull

injuries.description: 3 scalp lacerations over right fronto-parietal region with active bleeding.
source: There were 3 scalp lacerations over right fronto-parietal region with active bleeding.
there were lacerations on his face and head, and he also suffered a fracture of the left rib.
the plaintiff admitted that he was born deaf in left ear

injuries.description: head injury resulting in symptoms of post concussional syndrome and post traumatic stress disorder ("PTSD"), and/or aggravation of pre-existing psychiatric condition.
source: It is the case of the plaintiff that he is now suffering from head injury resulting in symptoms of post concussional syndrome and post traumatic stress disorder (“PTSD”), and/or aggravation of pre-existing psychiatric condition.

manifestations.description: intermittent headache every afternoon localized over the right side of head lasting 6 to 8 hours
afraid to go to sleep at night / fear of strangers and public places
poor sleep / sleep disturbance / need for Ativan to help with sleep
difficulty in swallowing which cause choking especially with solid food
3 scalp lacerations with active bleeding (initial physical injury sign)
no permanent functional deficit or cognitive impairment (clinical finding)
problem in washing (difficulty with personal care)
ceased running, cycling, swimming, hiking and scuba diving (stopped recreational activities)
no sex in few months after the 1st incident

treatments_received: treatment at Princess Margaret Hospital including CT brain
admitted once in September 2008 for persistent headache
referred to and psychological treatment at Caritas Medical Centre from May 2009 approximately every 5 weeks
admitted to Pok Oi Hospital and later transferred to Tuen Mun Hospital and stayed in hospital for 10 days with 2 chest drains inserted
follow-up psychiatric treatment at Nethersole Hospital, Queen Mary Hospital, Western Psychiatric Centre, and Castle Peak Hospital
psychotherapy by Dr Valda Cho from 2009 to February 2013

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: He used to run twice weekly at least which had stopped. He used to do cycling, swimming, hiking and scuba diving, which all had stopped.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: He was in fear of strangers and public places; afraid to go out at night.
Difficulty in concentrating, memory problems, emotional distress, depression, agitation and anger outburst, recurrent and intrusive thought of the assault.
Problems with balance and memory caused him problem in washing.

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: No sex in few months after the 1st incident.
He was dismissed by the kindergarten while on sick leave and could not return to full time teaching; part-time tuition ceased after the 2nd incident causing loss of earnings.
